CHIEF COMPLAINT
Lung nodule found on imaging during workup for cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kyle is a patient who presented with a cough of three months duration that began after loading hay bales while caring for horses. He subsequently developed a cold and presented to his primary care physician. Chest x-ray was obtained to rule out pneumonia and incidentally revealed a lung nodule. CT scan confirmed the finding. The patient reports the cough has since resolved. He denies any current pain or shortness of breath. He remains active with regular biking and exercise.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current cough, pain, or shortness of breath. No fever reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis
History of smoking (former smoker)

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly for rheumatoid arthritis

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with breast cancer, currently doing well. No family history of lung cancer or other malignancies. No previous history of lung infections or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Former smoker, quit approximately 7 years ago. Patient reports feeling better after cessation. Active lifestyle with frequent biking and exercise. Maintains horses. Lives in an area with new rail-trail systems used for biking.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 124/76, HR 70, RR 16, O2 saturation 98% on room air, afebrile.
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no clicks, rubs, or murmurs, no extra beats appreciated.
Extremities: Skin pink, warm, and dry. No edema in lower extremities. Mild swelling of knuckles on third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. Pulses intact in all extremities with brisk capillary refill.

RESULTS
Chest CT: Solitary 2 cm smooth nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule. Plan to order pulmonary function tests for baseline lung function assessment. PET CT scheduled to determine if nodule is metabolically active. Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) recommended for nodule removal with small portion of lung tissue. Procedure will involve three small incisions, general anesthesia, and approximately one and a half hours operative time. Patient will be admitted postoperatively with chest tube anticipated to be removed the following day at bedside. Expected hospital stay of one night. Continue rheumatoid arthritis management with rheumatologist follow-up and continued methotrexate therapy as previously outlined.
